_readme: LISTENING TESTS
PLAYBACK. Each test is spoken by the browser's own speech engine unless it
has an "audio" field, in which case that recording is played instead:
"audio": "downloads/listening/l07-1.mp3"
Adding that one field switches a test from browser speech to a recording.
Nothing else in the test changes, so MP3s can replace speech one test at a
time whenever recordings become available.
MODES. Every test offers Practice (replay freely) and Formal test (the
recording plays twice only). The student chooses; the default is Practice.
Fields for each test:
id           used by <div data-listening="ID"> on a page
grade        6 to 11
rate         base speaking rate. Lower is slower and clearer. The
speed control multiplies this, so a Grade 6 passage stays
slower than a Grade 11 one at every setting.
instructions what the student is told to do
script[]     speaker + text. Distinct speakers get distinct voices where
the device offers more than one English voice.
questions[]  see the six kinds below
Question kinds:
mcq        prompt, options[], answer (position from 0), explanation
gap        prompt, answer (word or list of acceptable words), explanation
short      prompt, answer (or list), explanation
note       prompt, lines[] each with label and answer, explanation
match      prompt, pairs[] with term and meaning, explanation
sequence   prompt, items[] IN THE CORRECT ORDER, explanation
The transcript is built from script[] and is written into the page only
after the student submits. After editing this file, run build.cmd.

tests.title: At the school office
tests.description: A short conversation between a student and the school clerk. Competency levels 1.1 and 1.2 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple functional text and extracts the information conveyed.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation and answer the questions. Submit to see your score, the answers and the transcript.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a conversation at the school office.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Good morning. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: Good morning, madam. I have come to collect a form for the sports meet.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Certainly. What is your name and your class?

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: My name is Dilini Perera. I am in Grade six B.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Here is the form. Please bring it back before Friday, signed by your parent.

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: Thank you very much, madam. Should I bring anything else?

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Yes. Bring one photograph as well. A small one is enough.

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: I will bring both on Thursday. Thank you.

questions.prompt: Why has Dilini come to the office?
options: To collect a form for the sports meet
questions.explanation: She says she has come to collect a form for the sports meet.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dilini is in Grade six ____.
questions.explanation: She says she is in Grade six B.

questions.prompt: By when must the form be returned?
questions.explanation: The clerk says to bring it back before Friday.

questions.prompt: What must a parent do to the form?
questions.explanation: The clerk says the form must be signed by a parent.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about what Dilini must bring.
questions.explanation: She must bring the signed form and one small photograph.

questions.prompt: On which day does Dilini say she will bring both things?
questions.explanation: She says, 'I will bring both on Thursday.'

tests.title: A school announcement
tests.description: An announcement made over the school public address system. Competency levels 1.1 and 1.2 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple functional text and uses its information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the announcement. Complete the notes and answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to an announcement at a school.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Good afternoon, students. Please listen carefully. The inter-house athletics meet will be held on the twenty second of September.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: It will begin at eight o'clock in the morning at the main playground.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: All students must wear their house colours and bring a water bottle and a cap.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Students who wish to take part in the long jump should give their names to Mr Silva before Wednesday.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Parents are welcome. Thank you.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about the athletics meet.
questions.explanation: The announcement gives the date as the twenty second of September, the time as eight o'clock in the morning, and the place as the main playground.

questions.prompt: What must all students wear?
questions.explanation: The teacher says all students must wear their house colours.

questions.prompt: Match each item to the reason it is mentioned.

pairs.meaning: The teacher who takes names for the long jump
The day by which names must be given

questions.explanation: Students must bring a water bottle and a cap; names for the long jump go to Mr Silva before Wednesday.

questions.prompt: Who is welcome to attend?
questions.explanation: The announcement ends by saying parents are welcome.

questions.prompt: Apart from a water bottle, what else must students bring?
questions.explanation: The teacher says to bring a water bottle and a cap.

questions.prompt: Which event needs students to give their names in advance?
questions.explanation: Only the long jump is mentioned as needing names in advance.

tests.title: Meet my family
tests.description: A student describes the people in her family. Competency levels 1.3 and 1.4 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple informational text and uses the information conveyed.
tests.instructions: Listen to Sanduni describing her family, then answer the questions and submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a student talking about her family.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: Hello. My name is Sanduni and I live in Kurunegala. There are five people in my family.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My father is a farmer. He grows vegetables and he leaves the house very early every morning.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My mother is a teacher at a primary school. She teaches small children and she loves singing.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My elder brother, Kasun, is seventeen. He plays cricket for his school team.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My little sister, Ruwani, is only four years old. She is always asking questions.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: We also have a dog called Kalu. He sleeps under the mango tree all day.

questions.prompt: How many people are there in Sanduni's family?
questions.explanation: She says there are five people in her family. Kalu is a dog, not a person.

questions.prompt: Match each person to what is said about them.
questions.explanation: Each family member is given one clear detail in the passage.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sanduni lives in ____.
questions.explanation: She says she lives in Kurunegala.

questions.prompt: How old is Ruwani?
questions.explanation: Sanduni says her little sister is only four years old.

questions.prompt: Where does the dog sleep?
questions.explanation: She says Kalu sleeps under the mango tree all day.

questions.prompt: What does Sanduni's mother love doing?
questions.explanation: The passage says her mother loves singing.

tests.title: Getting ready for a trip
tests.description: A mother and son plan what to pack. Competency levels 1.1 and 1.2 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple functional text and uses its information creatively.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation. Put the events in order, complete the notes, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a mother and her son getting ready for a trip.

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: Nuwan, we are leaving for Anuradhapura tomorrow. Have you packed your bag?

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: Not yet, amma. What should I take?

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: First, put in two shirts and two pairs of trousers. Then add your toothbrush and a towel.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: Can I take my camera?

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: Yes, but pack it last, at the top, so that it does not get crushed.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: What time will we leave?

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: The bus goes at six in the morning, so we must wake up at half past four.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: That is very early. I will go to bed straight after dinner.

questions.prompt: Put the packing steps in the order the mother gives them.
questions.explanation: She says to put in clothes first, then the toothbrush and towel, and to pack the camera last.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about the journey.
questions.explanation: They are going to Anuradhapura; the bus leaves at six and they must wake at half past four.

questions.prompt: Why must the camera be packed at the top?
options: So it is easy to find
So it does not get crushed
questions.explanation: The mother says to pack it last, at the top, so that it does not get crushed.

questions.prompt: Complete: Nuwan must pack two shirts and two pairs of ____.
questions.explanation: The mother says two shirts and two pairs of trousers.

questions.prompt: What does Nuwan say he will do straight after dinner?
questions.explanation: He says he will go to bed straight after dinner because they must wake up early.

questions.prompt: Has Nuwan packed his bag when the conversation begins?
questions.explanation: He answers, 'Not yet, amma.'

tests.title: The lost kitten
tests.description: A short story read aloud. Competency levels 1.5 and 1.6 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple literary text and uses its information creatively.
tests.instructions: Listen to the story, then answer the questions and submit to see your score and the transcript.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a short story.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: One rainy evening, Tharu heard a small sound near the gate. It was thin and high, like a whistle.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: She took an umbrella and went out. Under the hedge, wet and shivering, sat a tiny grey kitten.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Tharu carried it inside and dried it with an old cloth. Her mother warmed a little milk.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: The kitten drank everything and then fell asleep in Tharu's lap.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: The next morning, a neighbour knocked at the door. She was looking for her kitten, which had run away in the storm.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Tharu was sad to give it back. But the neighbour smiled and said, 'You may visit her whenever you like.'

questions.prompt: What was the weather like when Tharu heard the sound?
questions.explanation: The story begins on a rainy evening.

questions.prompt: Put the events in the order they happen in the story.
items: Tharu hears a sound near the gate
She finds a kitten under the hedge
A neighbour knocks at the door
questions.explanation: The story moves from hearing the sound, to finding the kitten, to the milk, and then to the next morning.

questions.prompt: What colour was the kitten?
questions.explanation: The story says it was a tiny grey kitten.

questions.prompt: How did Tharu feel when she had to give the kitten back?
questions.explanation: The story says Tharu was sad to give it back.

questions.prompt: Why had the kitten run away?
options: It was frightened by the storm
questions.explanation: The neighbour says her kitten had run away in the storm.

questions.prompt: Complete: The neighbour said Tharu may ____ the kitten whenever she likes.
questions.explanation: The neighbour smiles and says, 'You may visit her whenever you like.'
